content: A denturist, also known as a dental prosthetist, is a specialized dental professional who directly constructs removable oral prostheses, such as dentures, for patients. In some countries, they are referred to as registered clinical dental technicians. Unlike dental technicians, denturists typically do not work under the supervision or instruction of a dentist. Their scope of practice is generally limited to creating removable prostheses, and they may need to refer patients to a dentist for other types of dental care. It is important to distinguish denturists from prosthodontists, who are qualified specialist dentists trained to create both fixed and removable dental appliances. According to the National Denturist Association, the responsibilities of a denturist include performing comprehensive visual or digital oral examinations and evaluations, which involve obtaining a complete medical and dental history of the patient. They also take impressions, record necessary jaw relations, select artificial teeth, and design the dentures. Denturists fabricate and insert the dentures into the patient’s mouth and provide adjunctive services such as repairs, relines, or adjustments of removable dentures. Additionally, they may supervise auxiliary personnel in the performance of delegated tasks. To become a licensed denturist, an individual must complete an accredited program, typically lasting two to three years, and have at least four years of experience and background in dental technology in most states and provinces. Denturism is the practice of creating and fitting artificial dentures for patients. It is a recognized profession worldwide, where denturists provide dentures and dental appliances directly to the public without the supervision of a dentist. The International Federation of Denturists comprises national organizations from around the world that aim to advance the profession and provide affordable, professional denture care to the edentulous population. In the United States, the profession is legal in states such as Maine, Arizona, Washington, Oregon, Montana, and Colorado, but it is illegal in others, including Florida. In Canada, denturism has been a regulated profession since 1973, with eight out of ten provinces currently recognizing it. The United Kingdom has also legislated the profession, where denturists are referred to as Clinical Dental Technicians. In Australia, the profession is regulated, and the Australian Dental Prosthetists Association serves as the national organization. A licensed denturist is distinct from a dental technician. While many denturists were previously dental technicians, they pursued additional education in denturism to expand their scope of practice. This prior training and experience provide denturists with a unique advantage, as they become highly familiar with cases of edentulism, oral anatomy, and landmarks, which are central to their work as dental technologists. Denturists are also distinct from other dental professionals. According to the International Federation of Denturists, university-trained dentists perform a full range of services related to patient dental health, including assessment, diagnosis, and treatment. In contrast, denturists focus on clinical work involving prosthetic devices and do not perform adjustments or alterations to natural teeth or oral tissues. Dental technicians, on the other hand, work in laboratories and are trained to create appliances for dentists but lack the technical training and legal authority to work directly with patients.
